method_note: FAST MODE, one round. WebFetch could not resolve Greek and embassy hosts in this session, so every page was read with Apify web-fetch. Firecrawl skipped (no credits). The two 2021 Ministry of Interior translation circulars are scanned PDFs with no text layer and could not be read; the 2019 circular uses a legacy Greek font and was decoded by hand (see F-028).

fx.note: RBA says its rates are not for commercial use; use them as an approximation only, with the date.

facts.claim: A marriage licence for a foreign national legally residing in Greece is issued by the competent department of the municipality of residence; the competent body for the procedure is the Ministry of Interior.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr, General Secretariat of Public Administration)
facts.use_note: This entry is for foreign RESIDENTS of Greece. Do not present it as the route for couples living in Australia.

facts.claim: Waiting period, exact wording: 'the mayor or the president of the community shall wait for one week from the date of submission of the relevant application for any possible objection by third parties'. Deadline of completion: 7 days. The licence is granted 'immediately after expiry of the one-week period' if there is no objection.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Say the Wedded Advisor confirms the current process. See F-032: the separate civil-licence entry gives 8 days as its completion deadline.

facts.claim: What starts the clock: the date the application is submitted. Staff check that all documents are present and that the newspaper notice has been published; only then is a protocol number issued. If documents are missing or conditions are not met, the application is returned with instructions and the procedure starts again.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Procedure steps 2 to 4. Safe wording: the week runs from a complete, accepted application, and an incomplete file is returned so you start again.

facts.claim: If a third party lodges a written objection (backed by serious evidence or a solemn declaration), the mayor immediately invites the applicant to contest it, and grants the licence after hearing them. If the licence is refused, the competent Magistrates' Court decides irrevocably within 10 days of the application.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: One sentence only, without alarmism.

facts.claim: Fee for issuing the licence to a foreign resident: EUR 18 (about AUD 29 at the RBA rate of 1 AUD = 0.6175 EUR, 12 Nov 2026). Paid as an e-paravolo, code 2386, by bank cashier, debit or credit card, web banking or Hellenic Post.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Write as 'EUR 18 (about AUD 29, 12 Nov 2026)'. The civil-licence entry for residents (F-032) says 'provided without cost'. Keep EUR 18 tied to the foreign-resident licence.

facts.claim: The licence is valid for 6 months.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Athens says the same (F-011).

facts.claim: Documents for the foreign-resident licence: a certificate of no impediment from the competent consular or other authority; a birth certificate translated into Greek; proof of residence in Greece; a passport, residence permit or residence certificate proving lawful residence; a divorce decree translated into Greek if relevant; the newspaper issue carrying the marriage announcement in a local daily of the municipality of residence; and the future spouse's passport or birth certificate.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Residents only.

facts.claim: Documents from Hague Convention countries are accepted only with an Apostille and 'translated into Greek by a Greek translator'.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Australia's DFAT issues apostilles (Australian-side facts belong to batch B).

facts.claim: Legal basis: Civil Code articles 1368 to 1370 (PD 456/1984); Law 1250/1982 (introduction of civil marriage); PD 391/1982 (civil ceremonies, licences, and certification of civil or religious marriages); Law 5089/2024 (marriage between persons of the same sex).
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)

facts.claim: The Athens Civil Marriages Department serves permanent residents of the City of Athens (Greek citizens, foreigners and refugees) and Greek citizens abroad who are registered in Athens. The applicant must appear in person with ID to lodge the documents; a third party with a proper authorisation may collect the licence. Online lodging applies only to Greek citizens living in Athens.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Athens
facts.use_note: Athens publishes no route for foreigners who live abroad, so a non-resident Australian couple is not served by this page.

facts.claim: Athens: 'The marriage license is issued seven (7) days after the submission and verification of the required documents and is valid for six (6) months.'
facts.publisher: Municipality of Athens

facts.claim: Athens: every document lodged must have been issued within the last six months; a home-country marital status certificate (the alternative to a divorce certificate) must have been issued within the last three months.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Athens

facts.claim: Athens, foreign residents: a marriage licence from the home country (if one is issued) with an Apostille, OR a Certificate of No Impediment from the home country or its Embassy in Greece, officially authenticated and translated into Greek; plus a birth certificate, officially authenticated and translated into Greek.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Athens

facts.claim: Athens newspaper notice: published in a daily Athenian newspaper (one copy per prospective spouse), giving the couple's full names, their parents' full names, places of birth, last places of residence and the municipality of the wedding. If one spouse is a foreign national, the details must also appear in Latin characters.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Athens
facts.use_note: No official source read says the notice must run 'eight days before applying'.

facts.claim: Australian Embassy Athens: each non-Greek citizen marrying in Greece needs a CNI, which both religious and municipal organisations require. The acceptable place of issue (the Embassy in Greece, a DFAT office in Australia, or another Australian mission) 'can differ significantly between organisations'. The application may be lodged with the Embassy in Athens or any DFAT office in Australia for issue in Greece. The CNI is issued in English.
facts.publisher: Australian Embassy Greece (DFAT)
facts.source_date: not shown; the page links to a retired smartraveller.gov.au/guide URL, which suggests it has not been revised recently

facts.claim: Australian Embassy Athens on translations: most organisations require all documents (CNI, birth, baptismal, divorce or death certificates) translated into Greek, and 'it is practice in Greece to accept only official translations completed by the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Translation Section ...) in Athens or one of Greece's overseas Consulates/Embassies'.
facts.publisher: Australian Embassy Greece (DFAT)
facts.use_note: SUPERSEDED IN PART. The MFA replaced its in-house translation procedure on 1 Sep 2021 (F-017, F-018). Do not tell readers to use the 'MFA Translation Section'. See the translation entry in needs.

facts.claim: From 1 September 2021, a simplified official-translation procedure replaced the old MFA procedure: citizens and public services choose a translator from the Electronic Register of Certified Translators (metafraseis.services.gov.gr) and contact them directly. This implements Law 4781/2021.
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Foreign Affairs

facts.claim: Certified translators on the MFA Register (decision P23MET-34908/19.07.2021, Gazette B 3149) work as freelancers and officially translate foreign public documents into Greek, provided the documents carry a Hague Apostille when they come from a Convention country. The minimum fee per page is set by joint decision (Gazette B 3903). You can search the Register on gov.gr at metafraseis.services.gov.gr.
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Foreign Affairs
facts.use_note: This is the current national route. No official source read mentions NAATI, so do not say NAATI translations are accepted.

facts.claim: The Ministry of Interior lists, among its marriage-licence reference documents, two MFA circulars: 'Abolition of the MFA Translation Service' (27 Aug 2021) and 'New system of official translation' (4 Oct 2021).
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Interior
facts.use_note: The titles and dates are confirmed. The PDFs are image scans and their text could not be read in this run.

facts.claim: Chania, foreigners living abroad: official translation into Greek, with names in Greek and Latin characters, countersigned by the Greek consulate of the issuing country, the MFA translation service, a graduate translator of the Ionian University's translation department, or a Greek lawyer (Lawyers' Code art. 53). Documents from Hague countries need an Apostille, and originals are required, not photocopies.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Chania, Civil Marriages Office
facts.use_note: The list predates or ignores the 2021 change (it still names the 'MFA translation service'). Use it only as an example of what one town hall states, and pair it with F-017 and F-018.

facts.claim: Heraklion lists who may translate: the MFA translation service, a permanent civil servant at the Greek consulate of the issuing country, a Greek lawyer, or graduate translators of the Ionian University.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Heraklion
facts.source_date: not shown (site copyright 2026; cites a 2007 council decision)
facts.use_note: Same caveat as F-020.

facts.claim: Chania, foreigners living abroad: bring an original marriage licence from your own country's competent authority, translated and certified, showing its validity period and naming the person you will marry. If it does not name the other person, the office will not accept it as a valid licence. Also needed: a recent birth certificate, a recent family status certificate (where your country issues one) and a recent passport copy, plus the municipality's application form and a Law 1599/86 solemn statement.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Chania, Civil Marriages Office
facts.use_note: No newspaper notice and no Greek licence or one-week wait appear on Chania's non-resident list.

facts.claim: Chania: documents may be lodged in person or by email (politikoi-gamoi@chania.gr), early enough to be checked, completed and signed so that the date and time of the civil wedding can be arranged.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Chania, Civil Marriages Office
facts.use_note: Originals are still required (F-020).

facts.claim: Heraklion, foreigners NOT residing permanently in Greece: a marriage licence from their own country, translated into Greek with an Apostille; a birth certificate translated into Greek with an Apostille; and 'a residence permit or VISA (whose validity period has not expired)'.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Heraklion
facts.use_note: No Greek licence, newspaper notice or one-week wait on the non-resident list. For the 'VISA' line, see F-029 and needs.

facts.claim: Heraklion, foreigners residing permanently in Greece: a CNI from their consulate; an apostilled birth certificate translated into Greek; a wedding announcement in the local daily newspaper PATRIS or NEA KRITI; a residence permit; and a fee stamp listed as EUR 15 ('in real value 18 EUR'). Names on the application and in the newspaper are written in Greek letters.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Heraklion
facts.use_note: The fee wording is dated and confused. Use EUR 18 from gov.gr (F-005).

facts.claim: Heraklion: each person marrying must be accompanied by an adult witness. The witness may be a relative, even a first-degree one, and must bring an identity card or, for foreigners, a passport.
facts.publisher: Municipality of Heraklion
facts.use_note: This means two witnesses in total. Other municipalities may differ.

facts.claim: Heraklion civil ceremony fees under City Council decision 906/2007: EUR 100 (about AUD 162) for weddings on Tuesday or Thursday at 12:00, and EUR 150 (about AUD 243) on Wednesday or Friday from 18:00. Ceremonies take place in the Municipal Council Hall (Eleftherios Venizelos), where a photographer of the couple's choice may attend. Rate: 1 AUD = 0.6175 EUR (RBA, 12 Nov 2026).
facts.publisher: Municipality of Heraklion
facts.source_date: fees from a 2007 council decision; still on the live page 2026-11-12
facts.use_note: Present as 'one municipality's published fees; confirm currency with the town hall'.

facts.claim: Ministry of Interior circular 1969/S.477 of 4 January 2019 ('Civil marriage in Greece between foreigners'): a foreign public document certifying that a foreign national has no impediment to marrying in Greece is equivalent to a marriage licence under Greek law when it also names the other future spouse, so a Greek marriage licence need not be issued ('parelkei i ekdosi adeias gamou'). The same circular says foreigners lawfully resident in Greece apply to their municipality of residence.
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Interior, Directorate of Civil and Municipal Status
facts.use_note: KEY FACT for 'do non-residents skip the wait'. Confidence is medium only because the PDF uses a legacy Greek font that I decoded by hand; a Greek reader should confirm the wording. It matches Chania (F-022) and Heraklion (F-024). Whether this applies depends on the Australian CNI naming the intended spouse (see needs). The Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Same circular (4 Jan 2019): an essential precondition for foreigners to marry in Greece is producing an official document (passport, visa, residence permit and so on) showing that they are lawfully present in Greece.
facts.publisher: Hellenic Ministry of Interior
facts.use_note: Suggests Heraklion's 'residence permit or VISA' means proof of lawful stay, which for a visa-free Australian would be the passport with its entry record. That last step is my inference and is not stated in the source; see needs.

facts.claim: Exchange rate: 1 AUD = 0.6175 EUR on 12 Nov 2026 (RBA, 4pm).
facts.publisher: Reserve Bank of Australia
facts.use_note: EUR 18 is about AUD 29. EUR 100 is about AUD 162. EUR 150 is about AUD 243.

facts.claim: 'According to the law, in order for the marriage to take place, whether as a civil marriage or as a marriage solemnised by the Eastern Orthodox church, a licence is required by the mayor of the last place of residence, of each of the persons to be married.'
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: The Orthodox route still needs the mayor's licence (or, for non-residents, its foreign equivalent per F-028). Church conditions are in needs.

facts.claim: The registry entry 'Issue of a civil marriage licence' (residents of the municipality, which can be done digitally on gov.gr) lists 'Deadline of completion: 8 days', 'Fees: Provided without cost' and 'Validity duration: 6 months'. Its steps are a one-week objection wait (P7D) followed by granting of the licence (P1D). If the marriage does not take place within six months of the newspaper notice, the notice must be repeated.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: IMPORTANT, AND THE BRIEF MUST CHANGE. An official gov.gr page does state 8 days as the completion deadline: 7 days waiting plus 1 day to grant. The legal waiting period is still one week (Civil Code art. 1369 as described on both entries). Accurate line: 'the law sets a one-week objection period; gov.gr lists the whole process at 7 to 8 days'. Do not say 'no official source says eight days'.

facts.claim: Civil licence entry: the details on the birth certificate, the ID and the newspaper notice must match each other; if conditions are not met or documents are missing, the application is returned.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Supports the 'spelling must match across documents' line.

facts.claim: A marriage certificate (lixiarchiki praxi gamou) presupposes that the religious or civil marriage has been registered at the registry office (lixiarcheio) of the municipality where it took place, under Law 344/1976. Copies or extracts are free, with a 10-day completion deadline. They are available from municipalities, KEP citizen centres, or digitally on gov.gr with TAXISnet credentials. The digital certificate carries an electronic seal and QR code and needs no further certification in printed form.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Visiting Australians generally lack TAXISnet codes, so plan on an in-person or proxy request. That is an inference, so phrase it as 'may'.

facts.claim: Same-sex couples: Law 5089/2024 (Gazette A 27/2024) provides for civil marriage between persons of the same sex and is cited as a legal basis on both gov.gr licence entries.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Civil only. No official church source read on Orthodox weddings for same-sex couples; do not state church position beyond 'not available' without a source (see needs).

needs.detail: The brief says 'No official source supports eight days'. That is wrong. gov.gr's 'Issue of a civil marriage licence' entry (F-032, updated 5 Nov 2026) lists 'Deadline of completion: 8 days' (7-day objection wait plus 1 day to grant). The foreign-resident entry says 7 days, and Athens says seven days. Recommended framing: one-week legal wait, about 7 to 8 days end to end on gov.gr. Strategist and title owner to revisit the title note and must_avoid.

needs.topic: Non-resident Australians: skip the Greek licence?
needs.detail: Nationally (Interior circular of 4 Jan 2019, F-028), a foreign certificate that names the other spouse is equivalent to a Greek licence, so no Greek licence is issued. Chania (F-022) and Heraklion (F-024) apply this for non-residents, with no Greek licence, no newspaper notice and no one-week wait on their lists. Athens publishes only a residents' route. UNCONFIRMED: whether the DFAT CNI names the intended spouse (check the Smartraveller CNI form in batch B). Thira (Santorini) and Mykonos have no findable official page; both searches returned nothing official. Ask the Wedded Advisor or a partner planner for current Thira and Mykonos practice.

Resolved by date. The Embassy page (undated, links to a retired DFAT URL) says only MFA Translation Section or Greek consulate translations are accepted. On 1 Sep 2021 the MFA replaced that procedure with the Register of Certified Translators under Law 4781/2021 (F-017, F-018), and the Interior Ministry's list includes 2021 circulars titled 'Abolition of the MFA Translation Service' and 'New system of official translation' (F-019; scans unreadable). Current national route: an MFA-certified translator from metafraseis.services.gov.gr, or a Greek consulate. Chania and Heraklion still list consulate, Greek lawyer and Ionian University graduates (F-020, F-021). No official source mentions NAATI, so do not say NAATI is accepted. Batch B to confirm what the Greek consulates in Sydney and Melbourne currently do.

Only search snippets (a municipal declaration form and an mfa.gr consular page) say a marriage is declared within 40 days; I did not read them in full. No mitos entry read states it. Late-fee figures conflict between snippets. Cut the number or verify it on gov.gr (reg.services.gov.gr FAQ) next round. Who registers a civil wedding (often the officiating municipality itself) is also unconfirmed.

needs.topic: Apostille on the Greek marriage certificate
needs.detail: A gov.gr apostille procedure exists (Hague art. 4 entry on mitos), and a search snippet says an e-apostille is possible only for documents issued through gov.gr. Not read in full. The issuing authority for apostilles on municipal civil-status documents (believed to be the Decentralised Administration) is not confirmed. Mark as a need, or fetch mitos 'Episimeiosi eggrafon symfona me to arthro 4 tis Symvasis tis Chagis' next round.

Confirmed only that the mayor's licence (or its equivalent) is required for Orthodox weddings (F-031) and that the CNI is required by religious bodies (F-015). No official Church of Greece or Holy Metropolis source was read on baptism, the koumbaros or sponsor, mixed marriages, or local Metropolis approval (for example the Metropolis of Thira). Commercial pages only. Use [[NEEDS]].

The 2019 circular (F-029) frames this as proof of lawful stay (passport, visa, permit). Reading it as 'the passport with entry stamp suffices for visa-free Australians' is my inference, not stated. Leave it out or say 'proof you are lawfully in Greece, such as your passport'.
Required for residents (gov.gr, Athens, Heraklion residents). Absent from the Chania and Heraklion non-resident lists. Not confirmed for Thira or Mykonos.
No official source found on whether an interpreter is required at a civil ceremony for non-Greek speakers. [[NEEDS]].

needs.topic: Ceremony venues outside the town hall
needs.detail: The Interior Ministry lists an NSK opinion 327/2003 and a 2015 standing mayoral act on civil ceremonies, not read. Heraklion holds ceremonies in the Council Hall. No official source read on beach or hotel civil ceremonies.
The EUR 100 and EUR 150 figures come from a 2007 decision but are still on the live page. Confirm with the town hall before publishing. Nic sign-off.
In this session WebFetch could not resolve en.mitos.gov.gr, www.cityofathens.gr, greece.embassy.gov.au or www.heraklion.gr. Apify web-fetch reached all of them.
